Central analysis (MDACC) --mode central is run by MDACC. It combines the exports (files A–J, see Export specification) received from the participating cohorts. It never needs individual-level data, and it runs offline from the same image as the site analysis. The run has eight stages: Stage What it does Files used Output folder Ingest Checks checksums, versions and file schemas; harmonizes alleles across contributions J, I, A, B, D, E, G, H central/ingest/ Nominal meta-analysis Fixed- and random-effects inverse-variance weighting (IVW) of every variant–feature pair A central/meta/ Feature level Combines per-cohort permutation p-values (ACAT); q-values; meta lead variant B central/features.tsv.gz Fine-mapping Multi-ancestry SuShiE in summary-statistics mode A (meta), C central/finemap/ Colocalization SuSiE-coloc and ColocBoost against GWAS summary statistics A (meta), C, GWAS central/coloc/ Interactions G×C and GxE synthesis G, H central/interactions/ TWAS inputs OTTERS / mvOTTERS input files and FUSION weights A (meta), E, fine-mapping central/twas/ Summary Counts per stage and enrichment of high-PIP variants in annotations all of the above central/summary/ A contribution is one study × ancestry stratum: an <ANC>/ folder whose status is mapped in the study’s *_cohort_I_strata.tsv. Contributions are numbered from 0 in ingest/contributions.tsv. Every meta-analysis table has a contrib_mask column, a bit mask over those numbers: bit i is set when contribution i contributed. Meta-analyses are run within each ancestry (scope = the ancestry code) and across all contributions (scope = ALL). Running it ./xqtl/run_xqtl.sh -profile seadragon -params-file central.yml --mode central central.yml needs only a cohort label, an output folder and the studies table. GWAS colocalization and annotation enrichment are optional: cohort_id: MDACC_central outdir: /rsrch5/.../xqtl_central_2026_11 central: studies: studies.tsv # required gwas_catalog: gwas_catalog.tsv # optional: enables colocalization annotations: annotations.tsv # optional: annotation BEDs for PIP enrichment fdr: 0.05 finemap: L: 10 coloc: pp_h4: 0.7 Every setting and its default is listed in Configuration. Relative paths in the three tables are read relative to the table’s own folder. studies.tsv lists one received export per study. export_dir is the folder that holds MANIFEST.tsv (export/<cohort_id>/ as written by the site): study_id export_dir COHORT1 /rsrch5/.../received/COHORT1_20261201/export/COHORT1 COHORT2 /rsrch5/.../received/COHORT2_20261215/export/COHORT2 gwas_catalog.tsv lists one GWAS per row. Each file needs GRCh38 coordinates, with either variant_id (chr:pos:ref:alt) or the columns chrom, pos, ref, alt, plus beta and se for the ALT allele; eaf and a per-variant n are optional. ancestry must be one of the ancestry codes used by the cohorts (AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR, SAS). For trait_type: cc, give prop_cases, the proportion of cases: trait_id path ancestry n trait_type prop_cases BW_EUR gwas/birthweight_EUR.tsv.gz EUR 298142 quantitative GDM_EUR gwas/gdm_EUR.tsv.gz EUR 180000 cc 0.08 annotations.tsv lists BED files (GRCh38, 0-based) to test for enrichment of fine-mapped variants: name bed placenta_enhancers annot/placenta_enhancers.bed.gz The input validator checks all three tables before any task starts: required columns, duplicate IDs, folders and files that exist, MANIFEST.tsv and *_cohort_I_strata.tsv in each export folder, GWAS trait types and prop_cases. It warns when only one study is listed. Receiving exports Keep every export exactly as the site sent it: the folder structure and file names are listed in MANIFEST.tsv with sha256 checksums, and ingest verifies every file. Put each transfer in its own dated folder, then point export_dir at the export/<cohort_id>/ folder inside it. A study that sends a corrected export gets a new folder; do not overwrite the old one. Ingest and harmonization Ingest stops the run (status FAIL in ingest_report.tsv) when: a folder has no MANIFEST.tsv, or any listed file is missing or has the wrong sha256 (central.verify_checksums: false skips the hashing, not the presence check); the exports do not share one export format: every study must have the same major pipeline version and the same restricted-file version; a study has no *_cohort_I_strata.tsv, or no stratum with status mapped; a required file class (A, B permutation, D, E) is missing, or a file lacks a required column. Strata that were not mapped (for example below_min_n) are reported as INFO and skipped. Different image checksums across studies give a WARN only. Allele harmonization. All exports use GRCh38 forward-strand IDs chr:pos:ref:alt with effects per ALT allele, so in a correct export no flips are needed; ingest still checks. For each site (chromosome, position and allele pair, strand-collapsed), the orientation used by most contributions becomes the canonical one. Other contributions are then: swap (REF and ALT exchanged): effect sign reversed, EAF = 1 − EAF; flip or flip_swap (opposite strand): complemented, and reversed when swapped; mismatch (alleles that cannot be reconciled): dropped. Palindromic SNPs (A/T, C/G) cannot be told apart from a strand flip. A palindromic site that has the same orientation in every contribution is kept, because the IDs are forward-strand. When orientations differ, the site is dropped from every contribution if its MAF exceeds central.palindromic_maf_max (default 0.4) in any of them; below that it is read as a swap. Frequency outliers. A contribution’s variant is flagged when its harmonized EAF differs from the N-weighted mean EAF of the other contributions of the same ancestry by more than central.freq_diff_max (default 0.2). Flags are counted in the meta tables (n_freq_outlier); flagged variants are not removed. Many flags in one contribution suggest a build, strand or sample problem at that site. Outputs: ingest_report.tsv (check, status, detail), contributions.tsv, versions.tsv, harmonization_summary.tsv (actions per contribution) and harmonization/harm_<chrom>.parquet (one row per contribution × variant). Nominal meta-analysis For every modality and chromosome in file A, each variant–feature pair is meta-analysed by inverse-variance weighting: fixed effects: β = Σwᵢβᵢ / Σwᵢ with wᵢ = 1/SEᵢ², SE = (Σwᵢ)^−½; random effects: DerSimonian–Laird τ², weights 1/(SEᵢ² + τ²); heterogeneity: Cochran’s Q with its p-value, and I² = max(0, (Q − df)/Q). The meta EAF and N are N-weighted means and sums. Splicing features in site-specific novel clusters (nclu_, novel = true in file E) are excluded, because their IDs differ between sites (Phenotyping). Output: meta/<modality>_<chrom>.parquet with scope, modality, chrom, phenotype_id, variant_id, tss_distance, n, eaf, k, beta_fe, se_fe, z_fe, p_fe, beta_re, se_re, p_re, tau2, q_het, p_het, i2, n_freq_outlier, contrib_mask. Feature-level significance Each contribution’s beta-approximated permutation p-value (pval_beta, file B) measures the evidence that a feature has any cis-xQTL in that contribution. They are combined per arm, scope and feature with the aggregated Cauchy association test (ACAT), which is valid under arbitrary dependence [1, 2]. Storey q-values are computed per arm and scope, with Benjamini–Hochberg as the fallback when the q-value estimate fails (qvalue_method). A feature is significant when q_acat ≤ central.fdr. For ungrouped arms, the meta lead variant is the smallest fixed-effect p-value among the feature’s nominal meta rows (lead_variant, lead_beta_fe, lead_p_fe, lead_p_re, lead_i2, lead_k). lead_concordant is true when every contribution reported the same lead variant; n_sig_contrib counts contributions with site q ≤ central.fdr. Output: features.tsv.gz. Fine-mapping Every feature that is significant across all contributions (scope ALL, ungrouped arms) is fine-mapped, smallest p-value first (central.finemap.max_loci caps the number). For each ancestry: z-scores are the within-ancestry fixed-effect meta z, adjusted for the variance explained (z·√((n − 1)/(z² + n − 2)), the susieR convention); LD is the N-weighted mean of the contributions’ signed in-sample correlation matrices (file C), sign-aligned to the canonical alleles. Because file C is stored as float16, the matrix is shrunk towards the identity by λ = max(ld_ridge, ld_ridge − 1.1 × its smallest eigenvalue). The variant set is shared across ancestries and must have LD in every contribution of an ancestry. Ancestries are added largest first while at least central.finemap.min_variants variants remain; loci with fewer get status too_few_variants_with_ld. Only variants in file C (MAF ≥ ld.maf_min, imputation R² ≥ ld.rsq_min at the sites) can be fine-mapped. SuShiE [3] then fits up to central.finemap.L single effects jointly across ancestries, allowing effect sizes to differ between ancestries, and reports 95% credible sets with purity ≥ central.finemap.purity. Outputs in finemap/: File Content loci.tsv One row per locus: variants, ancestries kept, region, preparation status status.tsv One row per locus: ok, no_cs or error, number of credible sets, run time pips.tsv Variant PIPs, PIP within credible sets, credible-set index cs.tsv Credible-set members with alpha and cumulative alpha corr.tsv Estimated cross-ancestry effect correlation per single effect weights.tsv Posterior effect per variant and ancestry (prediction weights, standardized scale) Colocalization When central.gwas_catalog is set, every fine-mapped locus is tested against every GWAS whose ancestry is among the locus’s ancestries. GWAS variants are matched to the locus by ID, or by the allele-swapped ID with the sign reversed; strand flips are not attempted, so the GWAS must be on the GRCh38 forward strand. Tasks with fewer than central.coloc.min_variants shared variants are skipped. Both traits use the same LD: the ancestry-matched N-weighted xQTL LD described above. No external LD panel is used. This is appropriate when the GWAS ancestry matches the cohorts, but GWAS signals in poorly matched LD can give spurious extra credible sets, particularly near the edge of an LD window. SuSiE-coloc [4]. susieR::runsusie is fitted to each trait with up to central.coloc.L effects (xQTL with sdY = 1; GWAS with its n, trait_type and prop_cases), then coloc.susie compares every pair of credible sets. When either trait has no credible set, coloc.abf (single causal variant) is used instead (method = abf). coloc.tsv keeps the pair with the highest PP.H4 per task; coloc_pairs.tsv keeps all pairs. A task colocalizes (coloc = TRUE) when PP.H4 ≥ central.coloc.pp_h4. ColocBoost [5, 6] (central.coloc.colocboost, default on). Multi-trait gradient boosting on the same z-scores and LD with central.coloc.M iterations; colocboost.tsv lists colocalization confidence sets with their purity, top variant and variant-level colocalization probabilities, or no_cos. Treat SuSiE-coloc and ColocBoost as two readouts of the same data, not independent replication. Interactions G×C (file G). For every lead pair × cell type, the interaction coefficients are harmonized and meta-analysed by IVW within each ancestry and across all contributions when at least central.gxc_min_contributions contributed (method = ivw); otherwise the single p-value is kept (method = single). BH q-values are computed per scope and modality. The central primary cell type of a pair is its cell type with the smallest q, if q ≤ central.fdr; otherwise unassigned. The maternal-contamination refits are meta-analysed the same way (maternal_* columns). Outputs: interactions/gxc_meta.tsv.gz and gxc_annotation.tsv.gz. GxE tier 1. Per modality × exposure × phenotype, the contributions’ adaptive-permutation p-values are combined by ACAT (p_feature_acat), with BH q-values over all phenotypes of the modality × exposure (q_feature_acat). The scope label describes agreement between contributions: Scope Meaning single_study one contribution tested the phenotype shared_concordant_lead several contributions, all with the same lead interaction variant; that variant’s interaction effect is meta-analysed by IVW (beta_meta, p_meta, i2) shared_discordant_lead several contributions with different lead variants; only the ACAT p-value is given significant_any and significant_all show whether the site q ≤ central.fdr in any or all contributions. Output: interactions/gxe_tier1_meta.tsv.gz. The BH correction covers all features, including single_study ones. GxE tier 2. Sites estimate interaction effects per SD of the exposure in their own stratum. For continuous, untransformed exposures these are rescaled to a common unit, the pooled SD over all contributions (gxe_exposure_scales.tsv), using the raw-unit SDs in file H. Variant-level effects are then meta-analysed by IVW per modality × exposure. The top variant per phenotype is flagged and BH-adjusted across phenotypes (q_top_bh, descriptive only, as at the sites). Outputs: interactions/tier2/gxe_tier2_meta_<modality>_<exposure>.parquet and gxe_tier2_top.tsv.gz. See Interaction analyses for the site-side tests. TWAS inputs The pipeline writes TWAS inputs; it does not run the TWAS. MDACC runs mvOTTERS separately. OTTERS / mvOTTERS stage I [7, 8]: per ancestry, twas/otters/<ANC>/exp_anno.txt (CHROM GeneStart GeneEnd TargetID, with the feature TSS from file E) and eQTLSumStats.txt (CHROM POS A1 A2 Zscore TargetID N; A1 is the effect allele, ALT). Z-scores are the within-ancestry fixed-effect meta z. TargetID is <modality>:<phenotype_id>. central.twas.features chooses the significant features (default) or all features. FUSION weights [9] from SuShiE: twas/fusion/<ANC>/WEIGHTS/<modality>_<phenotype>.wgt.RDat and <ANC>.pos. Each .wgt.RDat holds wgt.matrix (one column, sushie), snps (PLINK .bim layout, SNP IDs chr:pos:ref:alt, A1 = ALT), cv.performance (NA; no cross-validation), hsq (NA), hsq.pv (NA) and N.tot. Run FUSION with --force_model sushie, and use an LD reference whose SNP IDs are chr:pos:ref:alt. Weights are written for every locus SuShiE fitted, including loci without a credible set (no_cs in finemap/status.tsv); their posterior effects are small, and you can drop them using status.tsv. Summary and enrichment summary/central_summary.tsv (section, item, value) counts contributions, individuals per ancestry, tested and significant features per arm and scope, fine-mapped loci, credible sets and variants with PIP ≥ central.pip_threshold, colocalized tasks, assigned G×C cell types and GxE scope labels. ingest_report.tsv and harmonization_summary.tsv are copied next to it. summary/pip_enrichment.tsv tests whether high-PIP variants (PIP ≥ central.pip_threshold; best PIP per variant across loci) fall in each annotation class more often than the other fine-mapped variants: Fisher’s exact test with BH q-values, and a PIP-weighted enrichment (share of total PIP in the class divided by the share of variants in the class). Classes are TSS-distance bins (≤ 1 kb, 1–10 kb, 10–100 kb, > 100 kb) and every BED in central.annotations. The background is the fine-mapped variant set, so these are enrichments within xQTL loci, not genome-wide. Caveats LD comes from the cohorts. In-sample LD is stored as float16 and averaged across contributions; with small strata and large effects SuShiE can report extra secondary credible sets. Review secondary sets with low purity or in loci with very strong primary signals before interpreting them. Variant coverage. Fine-mapping, colocalization and FUSION weights are limited to variants in file C at every site of an ancestry. Unequal coverage. A variant–feature pair can be meta-analysed with fewer contributions than its feature (k versus the number of contributions in contrib_mask), because sites filter variants independently. Exposure scales. Tier-2 rescaling assumes linear interaction effects in raw exposure units; log-transformed and binary exposures are not rescaled. One ancestry per contribution. Admixed individuals are assigned by the site’s ancestry classifier; the central analysis cannot revisit that assignment. What the shared files cannot support The files A–J are designed for the analyses above. Some analyses need data that do not leave the sites. They need a new pipeline release run by the sites, or, for pooled individual-level data, a separate data-transfer agreement (see Collaboration brief). Analysis Possible from A–J? Reference data and software provenance Everything a site run reads, apart from the cohort’s own data and the restricted file, is inside the image. This page records where each embedded file comes from, how it is checked, and how MDACC builds and releases it. Embedded reference data The image holds the public references at /opt/xqtl/refs. The build downloads each file, verifies it against a sha256 pinned in assets/refs_sources.tsv, processes it with the image’s own tools, and writes a checksum list, /opt/xqtl/refs/MANIFEST.tsv. That list must equal assets/refs_manifest.tsv for a release build to succeed. apptainer run <sif> refs-check repeats the comparison at any time, and bootstrap exports the list as refs_MANIFEST.tsv. its record number is pinned on the # ZENODO_RECORD= line of assets/refs_sources.tsv. Primary-source files (genome, chain) are downloaded from their original servers and pinned by sha256; their published MD5s were checked when they were pinned (genome a08035b6a6e31780e96a34008ff21bd6, chain 35887f73fe5e2231656504d1f6430900). Genome The MDACC signal list and splicing clusters in the restricted file were derived on a cleaned copy of the GRCh38 no-alt analysis set. The image ships the original NCBI file. During the build, fetch_references.sh compares the contig names, lengths and sequence MD5s of the shipped genome with mdacc_genome_contigs.tsv from the MDACC record and prints either genome: identical to the MDACC genome or the contigs that differ. Any difference is reviewed before a release and recorded in the changelog. Ancestry PCA panel Each site prunes its own genotypes (MAF ≥ 0.05, missingness ≤ 0.05, --indep-pairwise 1000 100 0.1) and intersects them with the 1000 Genomes high-coverage panel (chr:pos:ref:alt IDs). Shipping the full panel would add many gigabytes to the image, so the shipped panel is pre-filtered: biallelic autosomal A/C/G/T SNPs of the 1000 Genomes samples with super-population labels, duplicate IDs removed, MAF ≥ 0.05 in 1000 Genomes, then --indep-pairwise 1000 100 0.2. The looser panel threshold keeps more candidate SNPs than the cohort-side prune, so the intersection stays close to an intersection with the full panel. RNA-editing sites (REDIportal) REDIportal sites define the RNA-editing phenotype. The REDIportal paper states that its tables are downloadable and usable without restriction (Picardi et al. 2017, Nucleic Acids Research), so the MDACC record includes the preprocessed hg38 site list (INCLUDE_REDIPORTAL=yes). The file stays optional in the pipeline: if it is absent, rna_editing is skipped with a warning. A site can also pass its own BED6 of editing sites with --editing_sites to --mode prepare_references. Built at each site STAR, Salmon and IRFinder-S indices are tens of gigabytes and depend on the aligner versions, so they are not shipped. --mode prepare_references builds them once per site from the genome and annotation above, into site_refs: (Phenotyping). Not public: the restricted file xqtl-restricted-<version>.tar.gz holds the frozen leafCutter cluster set (clusters pooled across the MDACC discovery cohorts and merged across ancestries, junction coordinates only) and the MDACC signal list (lead and conditionally independent cis-signals of the MDACC discovery analysis at q ≤ 0.05 for nine modalities and both ancestry groups, as variant and phenotype IDs). It contains no per-sample data, but it is not published. MDACC sends it by email to approved sites; request it from Sean T. Bresnahan (stbresnahan@mdanderson.org), stating your cohort, the pipeline version and the approved agreement. The pipeline checks its version and internal checksums before use. Software All software versions are pinned (see containers/env/*.yml, containers/requirements-pip.txt, containers/install_r_extra.R, containers/build_irfinder.sh and the ARG lines of containers/Dockerfile). The exact resolved versions are in the image at /opt/xqtl/VERSIONS.tsv and /opt/xqtl/env_lock/, printed by apptainer run <sif> versions, exported by bootstrap, and attached to each GitHub release. Notes on the software layout: Two conda environments. Salmon 1.10.2 and the R/ICU stack need conflicting libraries, so the aligners (STAR, Salmon) live in a separate align environment. Both are on PATH; nothing changes for users. IRFinder-S is compiled from source (release v2.0.1, commit-verified) in a separate build stage. Java and Nextflow are a pinned Temurin 17 runtime and the self-contained Nextflow distribution, both checksum-verified at build time and exported to the host by bootstrap. GPU variant. -cuda images use PyTorch wheels built for CUDA 13.2 (cu132), the oldest CUDA build published for the pinned PyTorch release. GPU nodes need an NVIDIA driver that supports CUDA 13.2 (check the CUDA version shown by nvidia-smi). The CPU image runs everywhere and is the default. MDACC maintainer procedures Building the public reference record (once per reference release) Copy scripts/packaging/mdacc.env.template to mdacc.env (ignored by git) and fill in the input paths. Then, on seadragon: module load plink samtools scripts/make_public_reference_record.sh --env mdacc.env --out /rsrch5/.../xqtl_public_refs --dry-run # lists every input, or MISSING scripts/make_public_reference_record.sh --env mdacc.env --out /rsrch5/.../xqtl_public_refs Upload every file in the output directory to a new public Zenodo record (CC-BY-4.0 for the MDACC-derived files), publish it, then pin it and commit: scripts/pin_reference_record.py --record <record id> --files /rsrch5/.../xqtl_public_refs/files.tsv git commit -m "Pin public reference record <id>" assets/refs_sources.tsv Building the restricted file scripts/make_restricted_bundle.sh --env mdacc.env --out /rsrch5/.../restricted --dry-run scripts/make_restricted_bundle.sh --env mdacc.env --out /rsrch5/.../restricted This writes xqtl-restricted-<version>.tar.gz and its .sha256. The archive is byte-reproducible: rebuilding from the same inputs gives the same checksum. Send it by institutional secure email, or as an encrypted archive with the password sent separately, to approved sites only. Building the image and releasing a version are described in Testing and validation.

Testing and validation This page is for maintainers and developers. It describes the automated tests and their test data, the checks run on MD Anderson’s seadragon cluster, and how the image is built and released. Sites do not need any of it: they validate their own cluster with the smoke test (Validating a new site). All test data are either public or synthetic. The test cohorts use real 1000 Genomes genotypes (chr22) with synthetic phenotypes carrying planted effects: they check that the software recovers known signals, not anything about placental biology. The only real placental RNA-seq in the tests is 8 public runs of BioProject PRJNA820329, cut to chr22. Development environment scripts/dev_env.sh /path/to/env # conda/micromamba environment matching the image export PATH=/path/to/env/bin:/path/to/env/align/bin:/path/to/env/xqtl/bin:/path/to/env/irfinder/bin:$PWD/bin:$PATH python -m pytest tests/unit # unit tests scripts/check_configs.sh # every profile resolves nextflow run main.nf -profile local,dev,smoke --refs_dir tests/fixtures/refs_mini \ --restricted tests/fixtures/xqtl-restricted-test.tar.gz Rscript book/render_book.R # documentation site into book/_book tests/scripts/test_bootstrap.sh # bootstrap + run_xqtl.sh against a mock image tree -profile dev (conf/containers/none.config) runs every tool from PATH without a container. It is for development only, not for production runs. -profile test (conf/test.config) points every input at the test data below and caps resources at 2 CPUs and 6 GB; combine it with an engine, e.g. -profile test,docker or -profile test,dev. Unit tests tests/unit/ (pytest) covers input validation, the restricted file, reference download and checks, the MDACC packaging scripts, splicing clusters, mapping and export helpers (including the leak scan), G×C and GxE statistics, imputation preparation and the central analysis. The central tests compare the IVW meta-analysis with a hand calculation and cover ACAT, allele harmonization and exposure rescaling. test_docs.py checks that every cohort.yml setting in the schema is documented in Configuration. End-to-end tests Each script runs the pipeline on test data and then checks the outputs. Usage: tests/scripts/<test>.sh [WORKDIR] [ENGINE], with ENGINE = dev (tools on PATH) or docker. Site run: test_site.sh Test cohort tests/fixtures/site/ (built by make_site_fixture.sh and make_site_fixture.py): 130 1000 Genomes samples on chr22 with synthetic phenotypes and planted cis effects (TRUTH.tsv). The test runs --mode site with -profile test and checks that: the planted cis effects are recovered in EUR and EAS (q ≤ 0.05 in file B; correct sign and p ≤ 10⁻³ at the planted variant in file A; check_site_truth.py); AFR (n = 10, below ancestry.min_n) is listed in I_strata but not mapped or exported; a sample ID planted in a site output makes --mode export fail and leaves no export behind, and --mode export rebuilds the same export once it is removed. Interactions. The site cohort also carries planted interactions: a G × Cytotrophoblast interaction on ENSGFIX0000011; a G × GA interaction on ENSGFIX0000021 (planted variant chr22:20290948:A:G); a G × GA splicing plant on clu_31. The restricted test file (tests/fixtures/xqtl-restricted-test.tar.gz, built by make_restricted_test.sh) adds MDACC pairs that exercise every test-set flag: a phenotype absent from the site, a variant absent from the site, a different MDACC lead for a site eGene, shared pairs, and an MDACC-only pair. With GA and the maternal-age sensitivity enabled, check_site_interactions.py checks, in EUR and EAS: the primary cell type of ENSGFIX0000011; the tier-1 q-value and sign for ENSGFIX0000021; the tier-2 top variant for ENSGFIX0000021; the test-set sources and untested reasons; H_status; the sensitivity refit. It asserts only the planted pairs: with 60 samples per stratum, another pair can reach q ≤ 0.05 by chance. GxE recovery is checked on the expression plant only; normalization of splicing ratios attenuates the splicing plant too much to detect at n = 60, so that plant is checked only for its main effect and test-set flags. Central analysis: test_central.sh test_central.sh runs --mode site for two independent test cohorts, then --mode central. Cohort 1 is the site cohort above (parquet export). Cohort 2 (tests/fixtures/site2/, built by make_central_fixture.sh) has 120 other 1000 Genomes samples (60 EUR, 60 EAS), the same planted effects with other random seeds, and is exported as tsv.gz. The cohorts do not share samples, and each stratum has at least ancestry.min_n = 50 samples. GWAS. tests/fixtures/central/make_gwas.py writes a synthetic GWAS from one export’s LD window: one causal variant shared with a planted cis effect (colocalizing) and one nearby independent causal variant (a distinct signal, H3). The test adds a BED of the planted variants (±1 kb) as an enrichment annotation and gives study 2 as a path relative to studies.tsv. check_central.py checks ingest, the planted signals at meta, feature, fine-mapping, colocalization, G×C and GxE level, the tier-1 scope labels, the TWAS input files and the summary. check_central_ivw.R recomputes the fixed- and random-effects IVW (Q, I², τ²) in R from the raw file A rows of both exports and loads every FUSION weight file. Phenotyping: test_phenotyping.sh test_phenotyping.sh runs --mode prepare_references and --mode phenotyping_only (-profile test_phenotyping) and checks the phenotype BEDs (check_phenotypes.py). Reads. 8 public placenta RNA-seq runs of BioProject PRJNA820329 (Seoul National University Hospital), as read pairs with both mates on chr22 (tests/fixtures/fastq/, tests/fixtures/phenotyping/). extract_snuh_chr22.sh cuts them from STAR alignments and make_fastq_fixture.sh writes the fixture. Base qualities are set to a constant (Phred 30), as in SRA Lite, so base-quality filters act differently from real data. Annotation. GENCODE v45 chr22 (gencode.v45.annotation.gtf.gz, sha256-pinned in make_refs_fixture.sh), written in the HPLRv2 PANTRY GTF form and processed with Pantry’s txrevise scripts, is a public stand-in for HPLRv2 (tests/fixtures/refs_chr22/). Real runs use the HPLRv2 annotation in the image. Editing sites and cell types. refs_chr22/editing/ and music/ are chr22 cuts of the public reference record (extract_refs_chr22.sh): 413,357 REDIportal sites on chr22, and a mini single-cell reference of 254 chr22 genes and 3,857 cells (at most 30 cells per cell type and donor; 29 cell types, 5 donors). With so few genes, the test’s cell proportions only check that the step runs; they are not realistic estimates. Splicing. The test’s restricted file freezes every other leafCutter cluster of these samples (make_phenotyping_restricted.sh), so both frozen and novel clusters are exercised. The chr22 genome is cut from the image’s GRCh38 FASTA. On it, IRFinder-S writes an empty intergenic.ROI.bed, because it keeps intergenic regions only on chromosome names of up to two characters. This does not affect IR ratios. Imputation preparation: test_imputation_prep.sh Test data tests/fixtures/imputation_prep/ (rebuilt by make_fixture.sh): a 1000 Genomes phase 3 GRCh37 chr22 slice of 40 site-cohort samples, chr22 hg19 → hg38 chains, and a GRCh38 PLINK set with REF = major allele. The test checks: GRCh37 VCF → liftover → chr22.vcf.gz at the GRCh38 positions and alleles of the same samples’ GRCh38 genotypes, plus the report, liftover summary and TOPMed checklist; GRCh38 PLINK input → REF/ALT swapped to GRCh38 with genotypes intact; the GRCh37 VCF declared as GRCh38 stops with “Wrong build?” and publishes no VCF; duplicate sample IDs stop the run. Smoke test and bootstrap tests/fixtures/refs_mini/ is a small stand-in reference set (labelled “TEST FIXTURE: not real reference data”) for running --mode smoke outside the image. test_bootstrap.sh runs containers/bootstrap.sh and the generated run_xqtl.sh against a directory mock of the image, with the pinned Java runtime and Nextflow downloaded and verified as in the image build. Continuous integration .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on every push and pull request: unit tests, with dependencies at the image versions (tests/requirements-ci.txt) and again with the latest pandas, pyarrow and numpy; configs and linters: every profile resolves (scripts/check_configs.sh), nextflow lint, executable bits, shellcheck, hadolint and actionlint; image checks in the development image ghcr.io/sbresnahan/placenta-xqtl-federated:dev: versions, refs-check, the smoke test, and the site, central, phenotyping and imputation-preparation tests above. These steps are skipped, with a notice, while no development image is published. .github/workflows/image.yml builds the development image on pushes to main that change the image inputs, and the release images on version tags (see below). .github/workflows/docs.yml renders the documentation site. Building and releasing Building an image containers/build_image.sh downloads and verifies the references, renders this documentation if needed, and runs docker buildx build with the right build contexts and arguments: containers/build_image.sh # development build (unpinned rows allowed) containers/build_image.sh --variant cuda # GPU variant containers/build_image.sh --release # every row pinned; references must equal assets/refs_manifest.tsv Releasing a version Pin the public reference record (Reference data) and push to main. The image workflow builds ghcr.io/sbresnahan/placenta-xqtl-federated:dev and uploads refs_MANIFEST.tsv as an artifact. Commit that file as assets/refs_manifest.tsv whenever a reference changes. Set manifest.version in nextflow.config, update the changelog, and push the tag v<version>. The workflow then builds the CPU and -cuda images in strict mode, pushes them, builds the .sif, pushes it to ghcr.io/sbresnahan/xqtl-federated-sif:<version> (pulled with apptainer pull oras://...), archives it on Zenodo, and attaches the .sif checksum, reference manifest and version list to the GitHub release. Release checklist (in order): All CI checks pass on main. Versions follow semantic versioning: a change in the export format (files A–J) or in the restricted-file version is a major version change. 1.0.0 (unreleased) First release. Export: files A–J with a mandatory leak scan (Export specification). Exports record the pipeline version (the export format is tied to the major version) and use restricted-file version 1. Central analysis: allele harmonization, fixed- and random-effects meta-analysis, feature-level ACAT, SuShiE multi-ancestry fine-mapping, colocalization (SuSiE-coloc, ColocBoost), G×C and GxE synthesis, TWAS inputs (OTTERS, FUSION) and PIP enrichment (Central analysis). Distribution: one offline image (software, public references, Java runtime, Nextflow, pipeline code and documentation), as a Docker image and an Apptainer .sif; bootstrap exports the launcher. Profiles for LSF, SLURM, PBS Pro, Torque, SGE and local runs, plus the built-in seadragon profile. GPU: the CUDA image uses PyTorch cu132 wheels, so GPU nodes need a driver that supports CUDA 13.2.
